extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians (graduate students, postdocs, researchers) interested in deepening mastery of their field
extracted.subtask_short: learning and relearning a math field
extracted.subtask_description: Advice on how to deepen understanding of key results and internalise a mathematical subfield, aimed at students and researchers; includes specific questions to ask about lemmas, proofs, examples, generalisations, and suggested activities (teaching, exposition, citation searches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeply understand statements and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Just because you know a statement and proof of Fundamental Lemma X, you shouldn’t take that lemma for granted; instead, you should dig deeper until you really understand what the lemma is all about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do more than record the proof; interrogate the result to internalise it so you can use it effortlessly and free up mental space to learn more material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find alternate proofs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking different proofs can reveal different perspectives, techniques, or simplifications; alternate proofs may generalise differently or highlight different themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare multiple proofs for equivalence and differences
rubrics_metrics.description: If you know two proofs of the lemma, do you know to what extent the proofs are equivalent? Do they generalise in different ways? What themes do the proofs have in common? What are the other relative strengths and weaknesses of the two proofs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse equivalences, generalisation patterns, shared techniques, and relative advantages to understand when each proof is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand necessity of hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you know why each of the hypotheses are necessary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check which assumptions can be removed or weakened and identify counterexamples showing necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalogue known, conjectured, and heuristic generalisations
rubrics_metrics.description: What kind of generalizations are known/conjectured/heuristic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey the literature and folklore to locate extensions, conjectures, and heuristic frameworks that place the result in a broader context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek weaker or simpler versions useful for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there weaker and simpler versions which can suffice for some applications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify streamlined or less technical variants of the result that are easier to apply in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect model examples demonstrating the lemma in action
rubrics_metrics.description: What are some model examples demonstrating that lemma in action?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile illustrative examples and counterexamples to develop intuition about applicability and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know when to use (and not use) the lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: When is it a good idea to use the lemma, and when isn’t it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the lemma's domain of usefulness and common pitfalls or misuses in problem-solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify types of problems the lemma can and cannot solve
rubrics_metrics.description: What kind of problems can it solve, and what kind of problems are beyond its ability to assist with?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map the lemma onto problem classes to know where it yields progress and where other tools are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for analogues in other areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there analogues of that lemma in other areas of mathematics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for corresponding statements, techniques, or philosophies in neighbouring fields to transfer ideas or import methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the lemma in wider paradigms or programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the lemma fit into a wider paradigm or program?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand conceptual frameworks or larger projects that the lemma contributes to, which can guide research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach or write exposition to internalise material
rubrics_metrics.description: It is particularly useful to lecture on your field, or write lecture notes or other expository material, even if it is just for your own personal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching and exposition force you to distill and shorthand difficult results, improving ability in the field and freeing mental space to learn more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform citation searches for a key paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a key paper in that field, and perform a citation search on that paper (i.e. search for other papers that cite the key paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tools like MathSciNet or web search to find follow-up work, applications, and related developments you might otherwise miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate connections between problems and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: A good teacher should understand and impress on his students the view that mathematical problems have connections with each other and with other areas; we have a natural opportunity to investigate the connections of a problem when looking back at its solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After solving a problem, reflect on links to other problems, thematic similarities, and cross-disciplinary relevance instead of treating problems as isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask elementary or 'dumb' questions to probe understanding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asking simple, possibly naive questions about definitions, examples, and boundaries can reveal misunderstandings and deepen comprehension.
